A Port St. Lucie man has been sentenced to nearly four years in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate a popular online streamer as part of a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that authorities say cost victims about $260,000.David Anthony Sanchez, 36, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.Federal prosecutors said Sanchez, who also went by "Dave the Jewler," "Rueben Alexis De Jesus Santana" and other aliases, impersonated online streamer N3ON to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse and participate in it.According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3ON and communicated with the project's organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative.Prosecutors said Sanchez also executed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent organizers an AI-generated voice recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation.Believing the representations were legitimate, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts controlled by Sanchez, according to prosecutors.Authorities said Sanchez later converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the source and ownership of the money. Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit."Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in the release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money.In addition to his 47-month prison sentence, Sanchez was ordered to pay restitution to the victims. The amount of restitution was not specified in the release.The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

St. Lucie County commissioners are scheduled to consider adopting the final draft of the 2026 Port of Fort Pierce Master Plan during their Dec. 1 meeting. County Port, Inlet and Beaches staff will present the plan at the meeting, which begins at 6 p.m. Commissioners can ask questions and approve the document as presented or amend it before adoption, according to the county. The update builds on the port’s 2020 master plan and incorporates feedback from residents and industry stakeholders since commissioners last reviewed the draft on Aug. 11. The plan is intended to guide future development and help the county seek state and federal grants for port improvements. Among the long-term opportunities in the draft is a Launch Vehicle Recovery Facility to support offshore rocket recovery operations, including drone ships and other support vessels. As CBS12 previously reported, the proposed facility could position Fort Pierce to support recovery work tied to Florida’s growing space industry . The plan describes it as one part of a broader working waterfront vision, alongside mega-yacht services, marine research and workforce training, recreation and public access. The rocket-recovery proposal is one part of a broader vision for the Port of Fort Pierce as a mixed-use working waterfront. The plan also outlines Harbour Pointe as a public-facing district, with a regional boat ramp, waterfront dining and commercial space, an entertainment pavilion, a shared-use path and a living shoreline. The update also envisions a marine research and workforce training campus focused on marine science, environmental education and training for waterfront jobs. It calls for continued growth of the port’s mega-yacht maintenance and repair operations, as well as a marina at Museum Pointe where yachts could dock temporarily for crew changes, provisioning or staging before service. The plan includes infrastructure and access projects, such as a new road to Harbour Pointe, stormwater improvements and a possible connection to the regional Sun Trail. It also proposes a future Port to Park link to improve access between the waterfront and Franklin Park. See also: 3 auto insurers directed to refund $122 million in excess profits to Florida customers The 2026 update supplements the port’s 2020 master plan rather than replacing it. The document lays out a long-term vision for development; proposed zoning changes and the Port Overlay District remain under discussion. The county says commissioners will consider the plan during their regular meeting in the Commission Chambers on the third floor of the Roger Poitras Administration Annex, 2300 Virginia Ave. in Fort Pierce. The meeting will also be streamed on the county’s website and YouTube channel. Residents can review the draft plan on the county’s Port Master Plan webpage .

Cars were still getting through when CBS12 News reached one of the spots Port St. Lucie police had flagged for high water Thursday. Water pooled along Port St. Lucie Boulevard, and nearby driveways were dry. Earlier, water had made a lane impassable in two places on Village Parkway, and crews were pumping it off Tradition Parkway. Two weeks ago, floodwater stranded drivers across the city. Near Oak Hammock K 8, video showed a mother and daughter wading through chest-deep water. One location in Port St. Lucie recorded 16.7 inches of rain over 60 hours during that storm. Where police reported flooding Port St. Lucie Boulevard: Crews were putting up barricades at McCorkle Avenue, at Alcantara Boulevard and along the stretch from Southwest Liberty Drive to Firestone. Northbound Village Parkway: The right lane was impassable south of the fire station and south of Discovery Way. Water was spreading into a second lane near Discovery Way. Tradition Parkway east of Hazel Drive: Crews were pumping water off the road after the outside lanes flooded in both directions. Police said more closures could be needed as rain continued. The Florida Department of Transportation also had overnight closures scheduled this week on Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Southwest Fisherman and Southwest Liberty avenues for drainage work tied to a widening project. Where to fill sandbags St. Lucie County says sand is still available while supplies last at the St. Lucie County Fairgrounds’ west parking lot, 15601 W. Midway Road in Fort Pierce. The Lawnwood Stadium site has run out. The fairgrounds site is self-service. Bring a shovel and plan to fill your own bags. The county has a limited supply of bags and encourages residents to bring their own. Residents in unincorporated St. Lucie County can report flooding that threatens homes, businesses or personal safety to flooding@stlucieco.gov. What was different this time Port St. Lucie crews started lowering water levels in stormwater basins Sunday to make room for more rain. They also cleared drains and checked canals and culverts. A lot of it just depends on how much rain you get at a given time, city spokesperson Scott Samples said. During the Nov. 1 3 storm, Samples said, rain came down so quickly that the drainage system needed longer to move it. This week, he said, less rain had fallen all at once. We’ve been fortunate that so far we haven’t had that kind of rain, he said. Samples said homeowners associations and community development districts manage drainage in parts of Tradition. The city helped pump water out of a neighborhood there after the first storm, he said. It’s really a very collective stormwater system. A flood watch remains in effect for St. Lucie County through 7 p.m. Friday. The National Weather Service issued a separate advisory Thursday morning after radar and gauges indicated 2 to 4 inches had fallen across parts of northeastern St. Lucie County and eastern Indian River County. forecast.weather.gov See also: Who’s responsible for improving drainage after St. Lucie County’s historic flooding? Aftercare, sports and other activities were scheduled to resume. The district said weather-related absences would be excused with a note from a parent or guardian. In neighboring Indian River County, public schools and district offices were closed Thursday. More rain on already-soaked ground A flood watch covers St. Lucie County through 7 p.m. Friday. Health officials are warning swimmers to avoid water-related activities at several locations along the Treasure Coast due to elevated bacteria levels following recent heavy rain and flooding. Jetty Park Beach in Fort Pierce is among the affected areas, where advisory signs have been posted to alert visitors. "Heavy amounts of rain that we've experienced here in St. Lucie County, really here on the Treasure Coast, have resulted in higher bacteria levels in our waterways," Erick Gill, Communications Director at St. Lucie County Board of County Commissioners said. The Florida Department of Health reported that tests conducted Monday revealed enterococcus bacteria levels exceeding state guidelines at eight locations in St. Lucie County and three in Martin County. "A lot of it is the heavy rainfall and the runoff that we're getting, and agricultural as well as some septic tanks that may have been impacted by the amount of rain and flooding that we've gotten over the last couple of weeks," Gill said. Health officials are advising against swimming and other water-related activities at the affected locations due to an increased risk of illness. For some beach visitors, like Enma Kennedy, the advisories are not a deterrent to enjoying the scenery. "We get to enjoy it regardless of what's going. We have family that just flew in yesterday from California, their first time here, and look where we are. Rather rain or shine, we're here," Kennedy said. In St. Lucie County, advisories remain in effect at Jetty Park Beach, South Beach Causeway, Little Jim Bridge, Jaycee Park, Surfside Park, Walton Rocks Beach, Blue Heron, and Frederick Douglass Memorial Park. Health officials said the advisories will remain in place until bacteria levels fall below accepted health standards. Gill is also warning everyone to be look out for fire ants. "In addition to the bacteria levels residents should be aware that there are a lot of fire ants out there and other wildlife out there that might be seeking drier grounds so be cautious, when you're out hiking or playing in the back yard because fire ants are seeking shelter as well," Gill said. Small Business Saturday is just around the corner, and downtown Fort Pierce business owners are urging shoppers to support local stores as the holiday shopping season begins. Small Business Saturday was created by American Express in 2010 to get more customers through the doors of small businesses the Saturday after Thanksgiving. Small business owners in Fort Pierce are hoping you will shop small Saturday, and they're hoping you'll do it right here. The Executive Director of Main Street Fort Pierce, Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti and volunteers have been reminding business owners about the significance of Small Business Saturday. "Thank you so much for participating with Shop Small with us. Thank you, we appreciate it," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Juline Gurney, the owner of I Am Activeware, reflected on last year’s event, saying, "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be. I had many visitors, to be exact 19 visitors that day, and my sales paid my rent that month." Newcomer, Kim Brant, the owner of Sunshine State of Mind Boutique, is excited about this weekend's event. "Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be," Brant said. This is year number nine for Beryl Muise, the owner of Notions Potions candles and more. Muise says Small Business Saturday is the most important shopping day of the year. "So that is our busiest shopping day of the entire year for us. And with that, retail has a very short window to make their money for the year, and so Shop Small Saturday kicks that off," Muise said. Main Street Fort Pierce is hosting the event, and organizers emphasized the importance of supporting local businesses, especially as some struggle to stock their shelves. "For a small business, putting the merchandise on the shelf is the equivalent of putting food on the table. They can't be separated," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shopping locally also benefits the community, organizers said. "And remember when you spend a dollar in a small business, $0.68 of that dollar stays in your community. That gives the ability for your money to do more, spread wider, and have a longer impact," Chaffee Cavalcanti said. Shoppers will also have the chance to participate in a raffle to win hundreds of dollars in gift cards. The shops in downtown Fort Pierce will open at 10 a.m. Saturday, and raffle tickets must be submitted by 5:30 p.m. The drawing will take place at 6 p.m. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

Home Business News and Economic Updates in Sebastian, Florida Indian River County officials form Task Force 3 to help residents claim Amendment 3 property tax relief by Tina Hodges Nov 25, 2026 / 10:05 AM A A A A Reset Indian River County Tax Collector Carole Jean Jordan (left) and Property Appraiser Wesley Davis (right) Share on Twitter Share via Email VERO BEACH — Indian River County Tax Collector Carole Jean Jordan and Property Appraiser Wesley Davis announced Task Force 3, a joint initiative between their offices to help residents understand, qualify for, and receive the property tax benefits available under Florida’s newly approved Amendment 3. Voters approved Amendment 3 on Nov. 3. The measure makes significant changes to Florida’s property tax system beginning in 2027. Jordan and Davis said they are combining the resources, expertise, and public-service capabilities of their offices to help county residents navigate the changes. “We want to make sure every resident receives all the benefits they are entitled to receive,” the two officials said in announcing the initiative. Task Force 3 will focus on helping homeowners understand the new law, establish eligibility, satisfy residency requirements, obtain necessary documentation, and meet application deadlines. The effort will also assist real estate agents, title companies, attorneys, mortgage lenders, and others involved in property transactions by providing guidance intended to avoid costly delays or misunderstandings. “Carole Jean and I will spend the next six months talking to groups like the Board of Realtors, civic associations, homeowner associations, conducting media interviews, sponsoring town halls and speaking directly to individual residents, to make sure residents get what they voted for, said Davis. “We have established a technical committee of senior staff to collect, verify, and provide answers to the many questions people are asking,” Jordan added. People across South Florida and the Treasure Coast are bracing for yet another round of heavy rain , and one Indian River County community is pleading for help after battling repeated flooding this month. Joe Waters documented his frustration Saturday evening, recording on his phone in front of his mobile home in the Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach as a car drove through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights. Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, told me she wants to be a voice for her neighbors, especially those who can’t speak up. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said. The flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders, Carboni said. “We had a gentleman who needed EMS to come out, and they could not get to his home, so they had to park out on 82nd (Avenue), and then a large fire truck had to get to the home,” Carboni said. With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened. It’s horrible living in fear when you don’t know if it’s going to rain and you’re going to be able to leave your home the next day.” She wants to spread awareness about what her community is going through. “We need help, and we’re asking for help,” Carboni said. Emergency managers in Indian River County tell me they’re operating at a Level 2 emergency, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. They’ve extended the state of emergency through Sunday, Nov. 30. This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in prison for $260K AI cryptocurrency fraud
hero.body:
David Anthony Sanchez, 36, of Port St. Lucie, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison and ordered to pay restitution for a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that used an AI-generated voice to impersonate online streamer N3ON and cost victims about $260,000. Sanchez pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.

Federal prosecutors said Sanchez convinced organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that N3ON had agreed to endorse and participate in it. According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to look as though they belonged to N3ON and communicated with organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative. He also executed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent organizers an AI-generated recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation, prosecutors said.

Believing those representations were legitimate, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts Sanchez controlled, according to prosecutors. Authorities said he then converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the money's source and ownership. Prosecutors said Sanchez used the proceeds for his personal benefit.

“Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm,” Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in a release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money. The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit."Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in the release. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate victims' trust and take their money.In addition to his 47-month prison sentence, Sanchez was ordered to pay restitution to the victims. The amount of restitution was not specified in the release.The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

hero.headline: Stuart warns businesses of fake city invoices seeking thousands in project fees
hero.body:
The City of Stuart is warning businesses and contractors about fraudulent emails seeking thousands of dollars in development, building, planning or project-related fees. Several businesses with active projects and applications have recently reported receiving emails claiming to be from the city, with some recipients instructed to wire funds.

All official City of Stuart development and permitting fees must be paid through the city’s official OpenGov application portal. The city says it does not send invoices by email for these purposes.

One fraudulent email address reported to the city is commissions.stuartfl.gov@usa.com. The city encourages applicants with active projects to remain vigilant and carefully review all correspondence related to their projects to avoid being scammed.

cards.headline: Five taken to hospitals after Florida's Turnpike crash in Martin County; lanes reopen
cards.teaser: A truck hauling mulch jackknifed and struck an SUV Tuesday, sending five people to hospitals. All northbound lanes reopened at 1:56 p.m., according to the Florida Highway Patrol.
cards.body:
Five people were transported to hospitals after a truck hauling mulch jackknifed and struck an SUV on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County on Tuesday afternoon. All northbound lanes have reopened, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The medium-duty truck was pulling a trailer loaded with pallets of mulch. Both vehicles were traveling northbound when the truck jackknifed, striking a wall and the SUV.

Four people were transported to Florida Coast Medical Center, and one was transported to Martin Memorial South. The Florida Highway Patrol confirmed that the crash involved injuries.

The crash shut down all northbound lanes before they reopened at 1:56 p.m., according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The right shoulder remained blocked as of 3 p.m. Tuesday, according to Florida 511.
cards.article_text: A major multi-vehicle crash shut down all northbound lanes of Florida's Turnpike in Martin County on Tuesday afternoon, causing traffic disruptions for drivers. All northbound lanes were blocked, and the incident was classified as major. According to Florida 511, the crash is before mile marker 126 and mile marker 130. According to FHP, all northbound lanes reopened at 1:56 p.m. As of 3 p.m. the right shoulder is still blocked, according to Florida 511. The crash involved a medium-duty truck hauling a trailer loaded with pallets of mulch and a sport utility vehicle. Both vehicles were traveling northbound when the truck jackknifed and struck the wall and the SUV. Four individuals were transported to Florida Coast Medical Center, and one was transported to Martin Memorial South. Photos from the scene show multiple emergency vehicles and large trucks at the scene. Cars were also seen on the grass shoulder. The incident is classified as major. According to the Florida Highway Patrol , injuries are associated with the incident. hero.headline: Martin County meter-data problem leaves some customers with higher water bills
hero.body:
A water meter data collection problem dating back about five months left some Martin County utility customers with unusually high bills after previously unreported usage appeared on a single month’s bill, Martin County Utilities said.

The county said the problem affected usage reporting for some customers. After it was corrected, the accumulated usage charges appeared on one bill. Martin County Utilities said it has since implemented additional training and safeguards within its data collection software.

Customers with billing questions or who need assistance can contact Martin County Utilities customer service at cservice@martin.fl.us. The county said a customer service representative can work with affected residents to establish a payment arrangement.

hero.headline: Family remembers Alexis Cuellar ahead of funeral after Port St. Lucie hit-and-run
hero.body:
Alexis Cuellar’s family is speaking publicly for the first time about the 24-year-old killed in a Port St. Lucie hit-and-run as they prepare for her funeral service, scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce. Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work Nov. 16 when a vehicle struck her near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died Nov. 17.

At the family’s Port St. Lucie home, her father, Alberto Vasquez, and relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos and remembered her life. “Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun,” Vasquez said. He described his eldest daughter as someone who had cared for others since childhood, beginning with her siblings. She loved children and dreamed of working with them. Vasquez also remembered her time in Junior ROTC with pride.

Her aunt, Minerva Benitez, described the loss the family is grieving. “She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family,” Benitez said. Vasquez said the support the family has received has helped them through the first difficult days after Cuellar’s death.

On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched his daughter leave for her job at Wendy’s. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He saw her ride away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Vasquez said he wished he could have been there to help her and tell her he loved her.

Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer with leaving the scene. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He is accused of striking Cuellar while she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving. Additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow as police continue investigating the crash.

hero.headline: Heritage Plantation residents near Vero Beach seek help after repeated flooding
hero.body:
Residents of Heritage Plantation mobile home park near Vero Beach are asking for help after repeated flooding damaged property and complicated emergency access. More heavy rain is forecast, and Indian River County’s Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. Dawn Carboni, the community’s HOA president, said residents are frightened after battling multiple floods this month. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said.

Resident Joe Waters recorded video Saturday evening outside his mobile home as a car drove through floodwaters that nearly covered its headlights. He said wakes from passing vehicles struck and toppled bricks protecting his home’s undercarriage. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car remained in the shop with $4,600 in damage, awaiting insurance company approval.

Carboni said the flooding has created dangerous conditions for emergency responders. During one medical call, an EMS crew had to park on 82nd Avenue because it could not reach a resident’s home, she said. A large fire truck then had to reach the home. Carboni said she wants to speak for neighbors who cannot speak up and draw attention to the community’s repeated flooding. “We need help, and we’re asking for help,” she said.

Indian River County emergency managers said they are operating at Level 2, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated. The county’s state of emergency has been extended through Nov. 30 as the community faces the forecast for more heavy rain.

Waters said the wake caused by passing vehicles crashed into the bricks that protect the undercarriage of his home, toppling them. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car is still in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage, waiting on approval from the insurance company. When we showed up at Heritage Plantation Tuesday afternoon, a crowd of neighbors gathered — fed up after battling multiple floods just this month. hero.headline: Martin County meter data issue leaves customers in 10 communities with high water bills
hero.body:
Martin County Utilities said a water meter data collection issue dating back about five months left some customers in 10 communities with accumulated water charges on a single bill. After the problem was corrected, previously unreported water usage appeared on one month’s bill, resulting in higher-than-normal charges.

The issue affects some customers in Legacy Cove, Highlands Reserve, Cove Isle, Montego Cove, Emerald Lakes, Savannah Oaks, Cove Lakes, River Marina, River Marina Estates and Rocky Point, according to the utility.

Customers with billing questions or who need assistance can email Martin County Utilities customer service at cservice@martin.fl.us. A customer service representative can work with affected residents to establish a payment arrangement, the county said. Martin County Utilities said it has implemented additional training and safeguards within its data collection software.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie family remembers Alexis Cuellar ahead of Fort Pierce funeral
hero.body:
The Port St. Lucie family of Alexis Cuellar, 24, is speaking publicly for the first time about her life after she died following a hit-and-run crash while riding her scooter to work. Her father and relatives shared memories as they prepared for a service scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce.

Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was struck by a vehicle near SW Gatlin Boulevard on Nov. 16, according to police. She died Nov. 17. At the family’s Port St. Lucie home, relatives, some visiting from Texas, gathered around photographs to remember her. Her aunt, Minerva Benitez, described the family’s loss: “She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family.”

Her father, Alberto Vasquez, remembered his eldest daughter as someone with a natural instinct to care for others, starting with her siblings. She loved children and dreamed of working with them, he said. Vasquez also spoke with pride about her time in Junior ROTC. He said the support the family has received has helped them through the first difficult days after her death.

On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Cuellar leave home on her scooter for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He assumed she would be OK as he watched her ride away. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash. Vasquez said he wished he could have been there to help his daughter and tell her how deeply he loved her.

Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer with leaving the scene in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. Police accuse him of striking Cuellar while she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving the scene. The investigation continues, and additional charges, including vehicular homicide, remain possible.

hero.headline: Four arrested in attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club
hero.body:
Four suspects were arrested and charged with attempted home invasion Tuesday at Palm City's Evergreen Club, and the Martin County Sheriff's Office is asking residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. The suspects, three men and a 16-year-old boy from Jacksonville, are being held in the Martin County Jail without bond. Anyone who finds property missing should call the sheriff's office at 772-220-7060.

The attempted break-in happened around 3 a.m. at a home on SW Bimini Circle in the community off Murphy Road, according to the sheriff's office. A 17-year-old boy heard a noise outside and alerted his parents, who called 911, interrupting the attempt. Sheriff John Budensiek said the suspects tried to enter through a back door and covered a surveillance camera lens with a sticker. Home security video showed the group wearing dark clothing, masks and gloves.

Investigators said the suspects parked along a canal and walked half a mile into the neighborhood to target the home. When deputies arrived, the four ran in different directions, according to the sheriff's office. Deputies established a perimeter with help from the agency's aviation team and K-9 unit, along with the Stuart Police Department. K-9 teams tracked down all four suspects in separate locations throughout the community.

The 16-year-old was found hiding in a bush outside the community, and two men were found under a nearby bridge off Murphy Road. The fourth suspect was found in a nearby parking lot. Detectives believe that person was the getaway driver. The sheriff's office said at least one suspect was armed with a handgun. Deputies recovered masks, gloves and a stolen firearm.

The adult suspects were identified as Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr, 22; Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, 21; and Cameron Elijah Mapson, 21. All four suspects face attempted home invasion charges. Wise also faces charges of grand theft and possession of a firearm. Budensiek said three of the four suspects have violent criminal histories.

"These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going throughout their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. The group is seen on home security video around 3 a.m. wearing dark clothing, masks and gloves. hero.headline: FEMA aid opens for flood-hit residents in Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties
hero.body:
Federal disaster assistance is now available to residents affected by flooding in Indian River, Martin and St. Lucie counties, including grants for temporary housing and home repairs, along with low-cost loans for uninsured property losses. FEMA announced the assistance late Tuesday for individuals and families in those three Treasure Coast counties, as well as Palm Beach, Okeechobee and Brevard counties.

Residents who suffered damage or other losses should first file a claim with their insurance provider, then apply for FEMA assistance at DisasterAssistance.gov, through the FEMA App or by calling 1-800-621-3362. Applicants who use a relay service, including video relay or captioned telephone services, should give FEMA the number for that service when applying. The assistance also includes other programs designed to help people recover from the disaster.

Federal funding is also available on a cost-sharing basis to state, tribal and eligible local governments, as well as certain private nonprofit organizations, for debris removal and emergency protective measures. That assistance covers Palm Beach, Martin, Indian River, Okeechobee, Brevard and Hardee counties.

U.S. Rep. Lois Frankel said the declaration unlocks critical federal recovery resources for residents, businesses and local governments affected by the flooding. She said Palm Beach County officials estimate that $53 million in disaster assistance is needed countywide, including nearly $35 million for individuals and families, plus more than $18 million for local governments’ emergency response and cleanup costs.

Severe storms and flooding have affected parts of Florida since Oct. 31, prompting the state to request the federal disaster declaration. Additional counties could be designated for federal assistance based on the results of continuing damage assessments.

hero.headline: Four arrested after attempted home invasion in Palm City's Evergreen Club
hero.body:
Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, were arrested after an attempted home invasion in Palm City's Evergreen Club, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Investigators are asking residents of the gated community to review security footage and check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of an attempted break-in as they determine whether other homes were targeted.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when a family's 17-year-old son heard a suspicious noise outside the home and alerted his parents. The family reviewed security recordings and noticed one camera was not working properly. Earlier footage showed three people circling the house, Budensiek said. Someone had placed a sticker over a camera lens near the back door, blocking its view. The family called 911.

Investigators said the group parked near the C-23 Canal before walking into the neighborhood. Deputies searching a parking lot near the canal found the vehicle and took one person into custody nearby, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with help from aviation and K-9 units, as well as the Stuart Police Department. Two people were eventually found hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal. Budensiek said they were the last two apprehended after an extensive search.

The three adults arrested were identified as Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and Cameron Elijah Mapson, all 21. A 16-year-old was also arrested. All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to the sheriff's office. Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

As investigators retraced the route between the vehicle and the family's home, they recovered a stolen handgun with an extended magazine, Budensiek said. The sheriff's office also reported recovering masks and gloves during the investigation.

Investigators are examining digital evidence to establish why the four traveled from Jacksonville to Palm City and why the home was targeted. Residents who discover missing property or signs of a break-in are asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office at 772-220-7060.

cards.headline: Family remembers Alexis Cuellar before service after fatal Port St. Lucie hit-and-run
cards.teaser: Relatives are sharing their first public memories of the 24-year-old ahead of her Nov. 25 service in Fort Pierce. The driver is charged with leaving the scene, and additional charges could follow.
cards.body:
The family of Alexis Cuellar, the 24-year-old killed in a Port St. Lucie hit-and-run, is sharing memories of her publicly for the first time ahead of her Wednesday, Nov. 25, service. Her father and relatives remembered her as a caring eldest daughter who loved children and brought joy to those around her.

Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when a vehicle struck her near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died Nov. 17. Her service will be held at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce.

At the family's Port St. Lucie home, relatives, including some visiting from Texas, gathered around photos of Cuellar. Her father, Alberto Vasquez, said she had cared for others from an early age, starting with her siblings. He remembered her dream of working with children and said he was proud of her time in Junior ROTC.

“Alexis wasn't just a ray of sunshine, you know. I think to us she was just the sun,” Vasquez said. Her aunt, Minerva Benitez, described the family's grief: “She was the sweetest person ever, and it's a huge loss for the family,” she said.

On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched his daughter leave for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He saw her ride away on her scooter and learned five minutes later that there had been a crash. Vasquez said support for the family has helped them through the difficult first days after her death.

Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer with leaving the scene in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. He is accused of striking Cuellar while she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving. Police are continuing to investigate, and additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow.

hero.headline: Palm City family recounts attempted home invasion; four suspects charged
hero.body:
A Palm City homeowner said his 17-year-old son woke the family after hearing masked men trying to open their patio doors around 3 a.m. Tuesday on Bimini Circle. The father armed himself while his wife called 911. Four suspects are charged with attempted home invasion, and investigators are asking neighbors to review camera footage as they work to determine whether the family was targeted.

Three masked men, at least one armed, tried to enter the home. “My son heard them trying to jiggle open all three of our patio sliders fairly aggressively,” the homeowner said. After his son woke both parents, the father retrieved a rifle. “I grabbed my AR-15 and proceeded into the house as she called 911,” he said.

The homeowner believes turning off the outside lights helped scare the men away. “They must have seen me through the windows and seen the lights go out and left,” he said. He described the family's reaction: “We're a bit shook from the experience but doing good and feel blessed and lucky.”

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said his office deployed every resource it had to find the suspects. The search included aerial resources and K-9 units. Authorities found one suspect hiding in bushes outside the community and another near what investigators believe was the getaway car. Two others were found under a nearby bridge.

The Sheriff's Office identified the adult suspects as Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and Cameron Elijah Mapson, all 21. The fourth suspect is 16. All four are being held at the Martin County jail without bond. Budensiek said the suspects are from Jacksonville and three have extensive criminal records.

Investigators are working to determine why the suspects chose the Bimini Circle home and whether the attempted invasion was random or targeted. Authorities are asking residents in the area to check their cameras, cars and homes for signs of suspicious activity and contact the sheriff's office with information.

One suspect was found hiding in bushes outside the community, another near what they believe was the getaway car, and two others were discovered under a nearby bridge. The Sheriff's Office identified the suspects as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews, and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A fourth suspect is 16 years old. All four suspects are charged with attempted home invasion and are being held at the Martin County jail without bond. The sheriff said the suspects are from Jacksonville, and three of them have extensive criminal records. "These are bad, bad individuals who drove at least three and a half hours to Martin County to victimize a family that was going about their normal nightly routines," Budensiek said. One question investigators are still trying to answer is why the suspects chose this particular home. Budensiek said it's unclear if the attack was random or if the family was targeted. "We don't know the answer to that. We don't know why that house. We don't know if they went to any other houses potentially in the middle of the night," Budensiek said. Authorities are asking residents in the area to check their cameras, cars, and homes for any signs of suspicious activity and to contact the sheriff's office with any information. hero.headline: Four arrested after reported attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club
hero.body:
Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, were arrested after a reported attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Investigators are asking residents of the gated community to review security cameras and check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of another attempted break-in.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when a family's 17-year-old son heard a suspicious noise outside the home and alerted his parents. The family reviewed security footage and noticed one camera was not working properly. Looking through earlier recordings, they saw three people circling the house, Budensiek said. Video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door, blocking its view. The family called 911.

Investigators said the group had parked a vehicle near the C-23 Canal before walking into the neighborhood and targeting the home. Deputies checked a parking lot near the canal and found the vehicle. One person was taken into custody nearby, while the others fled, according to the sheriff. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with help from aviation units, K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Two suspects were found hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal, Budensiek said.

The three adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old also was arrested. All four face attempted home invasion charges, according to the sheriff's office. Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

Deputies recovered a stolen handgun with an extended magazine while retracing the route between the vehicle and the family's home, Budensiek said. The sheriff's office also reported recovering masks and gloves. Investigators are examining digital evidence to determine why the group traveled from Jacksonville to Palm City and whether other properties were targeted.

The sheriff's office asks Evergreen Club residents who discover missing property or signs of a break-in to call 772-220-7060.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie family remembers Alexis Cuellar ahead of Nov. 25 funeral
cards.teaser: Relatives are sharing memories of the 24-year-old killed in a scooter hit-and-run. The driver faces a leaving-the-scene charge, and police say additional charges could follow.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie family of Alexis Cuellar is speaking publicly for the first time about the 24-year-old killed in a scooter hit-and-run, ahead of her funeral service Wednesday, Nov. 25. Her father and relatives remembered her as a caring eldest daughter who loved children and brought joy to those around her.

Cuellar, known to her family as Lexi, was riding her scooter to work on Nov. 16 when a vehicle struck her near SW Gatlin Boulevard, according to police. She died Nov. 17. Her service will be held at Haisley Funeral Home in Fort Pierce.

At the family's Port St. Lucie home, her father, Alberto Vasquez, gathered with relatives around photographs of Cuellar. Some family members had traveled from Texas. Vasquez remembered his daughter's instinct to care for others, beginning with her siblings. He said she dreamed of working with children, and he was proud of her time in Junior ROTC. Her aunt, Minerva Benitez, described her as the sweetest person and called her death a huge loss for the family.

On the morning of the crash, Vasquez watched Cuellar leave home for her job at Wendy's. She had been excited about picking up more hours. He saw her ride away on her scooter and assumed she would be OK. Five minutes later, he learned there had been a crash.

Police have charged 18-year-old Tristian Ray Sanchez-Chasmer with leaving the scene in connection with the crash. Investigators say he had been playing ding-dong-ditch with friends before getting behind the wheel of a Chevy Tahoe. Police accuse him of striking Cuellar while she rode her scooter in a crosswalk, then leaving. The current charge is leaving the scene; police say additional charges, including vehicular homicide, could follow as the investigation continues.

Vasquez said the support the family has received has helped them through the difficult first days after his daughter's death. He said he wished he could have been there to help her and tell her how deeply he loved her.

cards.headline: Downtown Fort Pierce merchants prepare for Small Business Saturday shopping event
cards.teaser: Downtown shops will open at 10 a.m. Saturday as merchants seek support for holiday sales. A gift-card raffle drawing is set for 6 p.m., with tickets due by 5:30 p.m.
cards.body:
Downtown Fort Pierce merchants are preparing for Small Business Saturday, urging residents to shop locally as the holiday sales season begins. Main Street Fort Pierce is hosting the event, with downtown shops set to open at 10 a.m. Saturday and a raffle offering hundreds of dollars in gift cards.

For Juline Gurney, owner of I Am Activeware, last year’s event brought 19 visitors and enough sales to pay that month’s rent. “Last year I feel like there was a lot of new businesses, including myself, and downtown is a great spot to be. I had many visitors, to be exact 19 visitors that day, and my sales paid my rent that month.” Kim Brant, owner of Sunshine State of Mind Boutique, is also looking forward to this weekend’s event.

Beryl Muise, owner of Notions Potions candles and more, is in her ninth year and calls Small Business Saturday her most important shopping day of the year. “So that is our busiest shopping day of the entire year for us. And with that, retail has a very short window to make their money for the year, and so Shop Small Saturday kicks that off,” Muise said.

Michelle Chaffee Cavalcanti, executive director of Main Street Fort Pierce, and volunteers have been reminding business owners about the event’s significance. Organizers are emphasizing local support as some businesses struggle to stock their shelves. “For a small business, putting the merchandise on the shelf is the equivalent of putting food on the table. They can't be separated,” Chaffee Cavalcanti said.

American Express created Small Business Saturday in 2010 to bring more customers into small businesses on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. In downtown Fort Pierce, shoppers participating in the gift-card raffle must submit their tickets by 5:30 p.m. The drawing will take place at 6 p.m.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce boxing gym wins three state titles, takes second overall
hero.body:
A Future Worth Fighting 4 in Fort Pierce earned three state titles, a silver medal and second place in the team standings at the 2026 Florida State Police Athletic League tournament. The results gave the gym a chance to celebrate both its individual boxers and its performance as a team. For owner Darrion Henry, the sport is closely tied to the community the gym serves. “Here, this community is a big fighting community. If you’re from Fort Pierce, you know how we get down,” Henry said. That connection to Fort Pierce is part of the gym’s identity, alongside the training that helped its boxers succeed at the state competition.

Justice Henry stood out at the tournament, crediting his success to a gym environment that combines a sense of family with tough love. He has been boxing since he was eight, and his connection to A Future Worth Fighting 4 goes beyond learning the sport or preparing for competition. “This gym has been the biggest part of my life. I’ve been boxing since I was eight years old, and this became a home for our own little community and us, with everyone we bring in here,” Justice Henry said. His experience reflects the importance he places on the people around him at the gym.

Other boxers are still discovering what draws them to the ring. Frantzner Jean, a newcomer to boxing, won his first fight by unanimous decision. “It felt pretty fun; I just like the dopamine rush from it,” Jean said. His first victory adds another accomplishment to a gym where experienced boxers and beginners train. Children come in after school to learn boxing, but taking part carries a requirement outside the ring: They must attend school every day. Darrion Henry, who also teaches at Dan McCarty, said that expectation has helped change how some of the children approach school.

“I’m a teacher at Dan McCarty, so I can see how their behavior has changed, and now I have a lot of kids who show up to school because they know if they don’t show up to school, I’m going to get on them,” Darrion Henry said. Among the children following that school-first approach is Michael Sanchez. His father initially enrolled him in boxing classes, but Sanchez has since developed his own interest in continuing with the sport. He values what the training teaches him as well as boxing itself. “I ended up liking it because I can learn from it, like discipline and hard work,” Sanchez said.

hero.headline: Four arrested after alleged attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club
hero.body:
Four people from Jacksonville, including a 16-year-old, are in custody after an alleged attempted home invasion at Palm City's Evergreen Club, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The agency is asking residents to review security cameras and check their homes and vehicles as investigators work to determine whether other properties were targeted.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the incident began just after 3 a.m., when a family's 17-year-old son heard a suspicious noise outside the home and woke his parents. The family reviewed security footage and noticed one camera was not working properly. Looking through earlier recordings, they saw three people circling the house, Budensiek said. Video showed someone placing a sticker over a camera lens near the back door, blocking its view. The family called 911.

Investigators say the group parked near the C-23 Canal before walking into the gated community and targeting the home. Deputies checked a parking lot near the canal and found a vehicle. One person was taken into custody near it, while the others fled, according to Budensiek. Deputies established a perimeter and searched with help from aviation units, K-9 units and the Stuart Police Department. Two suspects were found hiding beneath the bridge carrying Murphy Road over the C-23 Canal. Budensiek said they were the last two apprehended after an extensive search.

The adults arrested were identified as 21-year-old Nathaniel Phillip Wise Jr., 21-year-old Za'kyri Isreal Emmanuel Crews and 21-year-old Cameron Elijah Mapson. A 16-year-old was also arrested. All four face attempted home invasion charges. Wise also faces charges of grand theft of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

Deputies recovered a stolen handgun with an extended magazine while retracing the route between the vehicle and the family's home, Budensiek said. The sheriff's office also reported recovering masks and gloves. Investigators are examining digital evidence to establish why the four traveled from Jacksonville to Palm City and why the home was targeted.

Residents who discover missing property or signs of a break-in are asked to contact the Martin County Sheriff's Office at 772-220-7060.

hero.headline: Indian River County extends emergency as more rain threatens flooded Heritage Plantation
hero.body:
Indian River County has extended its state of emergency through Nov. 30 as more heavy rain threatens Heritage Plantation, a mobile home park near Vero Beach where residents report repeated home flooding and difficulty getting emergency responders to homes. County emergency managers said they are operating at Level 2, meaning the Emergency Operations Center is partially activated.

Residents at Heritage Plantation have battled multiple floods this month. Joe Waters recorded a car Saturday evening driving through floodwaters that almost covered its headlights outside his mobile home. He said the wake from passing vehicles toppled bricks protecting his home's undercarriage. “The water came up probably about thigh high,” Waters said. “Came up into the driveway, went into the house.” Waters and his wife were able to clean their home, but he said his car remains in the shop with $4,600 worth of damage while he waits for insurance company approval.

Dawn Carboni, the HOA president, said flooding has also created dangerous conditions for emergency responders. In one instance, she said, EMS personnel could not reach a resident's home and had to park on 82nd Avenue. A large fire truck then had to reach the home. Carboni said she wants to speak for neighbors, particularly those who cannot speak up for themselves. “They just want to feel safe in their homes,” she said.

With more heavy rain in the forecast, Carboni said residents are frightened about whether they will be able to leave their homes after another round of rain. She is seeking help and drawing attention to the community's repeated flooding. “We need help, and we're asking for help,” Carboni said.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County mother accused of killing son found unfit to stand trial
hero.body:
Rhonda Paulynice, the St. Lucie County mother charged with second-degree murder in her 6-year-old son's death, has been declared unfit to stand trial and committed to the Department of Children and Families to determine whether her competency can be restored, court records show.

In May 2025, school resource deputies requested a welfare check after her son, Ra'myl Pierre, had been out of school for several days. His body was found on a bed, wrapped in fabric with only his face exposed, inside the Fort Pierce area home they shared.

According to a probable cause affidavit, Paulynice told deputies she had suffocated her son 12 days before his body was found. She told investigators she was trying to exorcise demons from his body.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man sentenced to 47 months in $260,000 N3ON cryptocurrency fraud
cards.teaser: David Anthony Sanchez was also ordered to pay restitution after using an AI-generated recording of streamer N3ON’s voice to help secure cryptocurrency payments from victims.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced Tuesday to 47 months in federal prison and ordered to pay restitution for a cryptocurrency fraud that used an AI-generated impersonation of online streamer N3ON to obtain approximately $260,000. David Anthony Sanchez, 36, pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.

Sanchez, also known as "Dave the Jewler," created fake online accounts posing as N3ON and his representative, according to federal court records. Through those accounts, he communicated directly with organizers of a cryptocurrency "memecoin" project. Prosecutors said Sanchez used artificial intelligence to create an audio recording mimicking N3ON's voice and falsely confirming the streamer's involvement. He also signed agreements using N3ON's identity, further convincing organizers that the endorsement was legitimate.

Believing they had secured N3ON's participation, the victims transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts Sanchez controlled, prosecutors said. Sanchez converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to disguise the funds' origin and who controlled them. Prosecutors said he used the money for his personal benefit.

U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian imposed the prison sentence and ordered Sanchez to pay restitution to his victims. "Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said. "In this case, the defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money."

The sheriff’s office is asking Palm City residents to check their homes and vehicles for missing property or signs of a break-in. Anyone who finds property missing should call the agency at 772-220-7060.

According to a probable cause affidavit, Paulynice told deputies she suffocated her son 12 days before his body was found. She also told investigators she was trying to exorcise demons from his body.

hero.headline: Sheriff renews unified dispatch push as Vero Beach weighs property tax cuts
hero.body:
Indian River County Sheriff Eric Flowers asked the Vero Beach City Council on Tuesday to reconsider merging emergency dispatch as a potential way to save money under Amendment 3, the voter-approved measure that will reduce non-school property taxes by increasing the homestead exemption. Council member Tracey Zudans requested cost and response-time figures. The council took no action on the proposal.

Flowers said he first brought the idea to the council about two years ago and that Brevard County has since moved to a unified dispatch system. He renewed his offer as Vero Beach prepares for revenue losses. “I'm not asking for anything specific today. I just want to make sure that it's known that it is my desire that we go to a unified dispatch system,” Flowers said.

Amendment 3 will increase the homestead exemption from about $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Florida voters approved the initiative despite a campaign by local officials warning that it would gut funding for public safety and other services. Flowers asked the council to consider unified dispatch as a potential cost savings while making budget decisions under the amendment.

Zudans asked city staff to quantify the proposal. “I'd love to see some numbers attached to it, not just response time numbers, but also some dollar numbers so that we can share that with our taxpayers as well,” she said. Flowers offered to have his staff work with city staff.

Vice Mayor John Cotugno asked whether a unified dispatch center would be a county function or operated by the sheriff's office. Flowers said the county technically runs dispatch, but most dispatchers work for his agency. He said the county would have to be asked about a different arrangement. The sheriff's office and county are still discussing how Amendment 3 will affect their relationship, he said.

The two sides clashed over the sheriff's budget in July 2025. Flowers sought $93.5 million, while the county recommended closer to $83.5 million. Commissioners ultimately approved a $6.8 million increase, and Flowers later sued the commission. On dispatch, Flowers said his goal remains bringing the staff together: “If we do it as a county, if we do it under me, either way, I'm just trying to get all of our dispatchers in the same room together.”

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man gets 47 months in prison for $260K AI cryptocurrency fraud
hero.body:
David Anthony Sanchez, 36, of Port St. Lucie, was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison and ordered to pay restitution for an AI-assisted impersonation scheme that prosecutors said cost cryptocurrency project organizers about $260,000. Sanchez pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.

Federal prosecutors said Sanchez impersonated online streamer N3ON to convince organizers of a cryptocurrency memecoin project that the streamer had agreed to endorse and participate in it. According to court records, Sanchez created online accounts designed to appear to belong to N3ON and communicated with the organizers while posing as both the streamer and his representative. Prosecutors said he signed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent the organizers an AI-generated recording that mimicked the streamer's voice to falsely confirm his participation.

Believing those representations were legitimate, the organizers transferred approximately $260,000 in cryptocurrency to accounts Sanchez controlled, prosecutors said. Authorities said Sanchez then converted a substantial portion of the cryptocurrency into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to conceal the money's source and ownership. Prosecutors said he used the proceeds for his personal benefit. Sanchez also used aliases including "Dave the Jewler" and "Rueben Alexis De Jesus Santana."

"Behind every fraud scheme are real people who suffer real financial harm," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said. She said Sanchez exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the victims' trust and take their money. The FBI's Miami Field Office investigated the case.

hero.headline: Four men taken into custody after Palm City burglary and overnight manhunt
hero.body:
Four men were taken into custody after an overnight burglary and manhunt in Palm City, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Deputies are asking residents, particularly those in the Evergreen Club community, to check their vehicles and the outside of their homes for signs of a break-in or missing property.

The sheriff's office confirmed at least one burglary in Evergreen Club. Deputies tracked four men wearing masks and gloves during the night before taking all four into custody, the agency said. The men are from Jacksonville, according to the sheriff's office.

Anyone who discovers missing property or believes someone tried to break into their home or vehicle is asked to call the Martin County Sheriff’s Office at 772-220-7060. The agency said it expects to release more information about the manhunt later Tuesday.

hero.headline: Flood watch issued for Wednesday as Treasure Coast rain chances increase
hero.body:
A flood watch has been issued for Wednesday, when rain chances on the Treasure Coast are forecast to reach their highest level of the week. Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms are possible.

Rain chances are expected to increase slightly Tuesday, with warmer temperatures on the way. The early-week forecast called for a mix of sun and clouds, highs in the mid to upper 70s and light northwest winds.

Partly cloudy skies and light northwest winds were forecast overnight, with lows in the low 60s along the Treasure Coast and in Okeechobee County. Palm Beach County’s overnight lows were forecast in the low to mid 60s.

hero.headline: Two injured in U.S. 1 tractor-trailer crash in Hobe Sound; one flown to hospital
hero.body:
Two people were injured Monday in a crash involving a vehicle and a tractor-trailer at U.S. 1 and SE Hobe Terrace in Hobe Sound, according to the Martin County Sheriff’s Office.

One person suffered life-threatening injuries and was flown to St. Mary’s Medical Center by Martin County Fire Rescue’s LifeStar, the Sheriff’s Office said. A second person was also injured in the crash.

The Martin County Sheriff’s Office and Florida Highway Patrol are investigating the crash, which the Sheriff’s Office described as a serious injury crash.
hero.article_text: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office , along with Florida Highway Patrol, are investigating a serious crash involving a vehicle and a tractor-trailer. MCSO says a serious injury crash involving a vehicle and tractor-trailer occurred on Monday at U.S. 1 at SE Hobe Terrace in Hobe Sound. Martin County Fire Rescue’s LifeStar flew one person with life-threatening injuries to St. Mary’s Medical Center, MCSO said. A second person was also injured in the crash. hero.headline: Indian River County Sheriff’s Office unveils memorial to two deputies killed in line of duty
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office unveiled a stone memorial Saturday honoring its two deputies killed in the line of duty, dedicating it on the first anniversary of Sgt. Terri Sweeting-Mashkow’s death. The roughly 10-foot obelisk bears her name and that of Cpl. Richard Raczkoski outside the agency’s new administration building in Vero Beach.

Hundreds of family members, fellow officers and community members attended the ceremony, which included bagpipes, taps, a three-volley salute, “Amazing Grace,” a rose tribute and the last radio call for Sweeting-Mashkow. The monument stands on the sheriff’s campus at 4055 41st Ave. The administration building is expected to open next spring.

“By placing the memorial at the front of our new administration building before we take occupancy, we ensure that every employee, every visitor, and future generations will always know the names and memory of our fallen heroes,” Sheriff Eric Flowers said. He said he hopes the agency never has to add another name.

Sweeting-Mashkow, 47, was fatally shot while serving an eviction notice at a home in the Bermuda Club community. She had served more than 25 years with the sheriff’s office, much of that time in patrol before moving to the civil process unit. Her death was the second line-of-duty killing in the agency’s roughly 100-year history.

Authorities said Sweeting-Mashkow was one of three deputies at the residence when Michael Halberstam, 37, opened fire. Deputy Florentino Arizpe was shot in the shoulder. Locksmith David Long, who was assisting with the eviction, was critically wounded and later died. Deputies returned fire, and Halberstam died the following day.

Raczkoski, 29, was killed Sept. 23, 1986, after answering a 911 hang-up from a phone booth outside a Zippy Mart on State Road 60 west of Vero Beach. During the encounter, a handgun fell from William Reaves’ clothing. After a short struggle, Reaves shot Raczkoski four times in the back as the deputy tried to run. Reaves was convicted of first-degree murder, sentenced to death and executed Oct. 20, 2026.

hero.headline: Two face felony burglary charges in Hutchinson Island game-room break-in
hero.body:
Two men are facing felony burglary charges after authorities accused them of entering a Hutchinson Island business after closing because they wanted to keep playing video games, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Sheriff John Budensiek identified the suspects as Ferdinand Schoedinger IV, 29, of New Hampshire, and James Bolon, 33, of Ohio. The incident happened late Saturday into early Sunday at the Indian River Plantation Shopping Plaza. Authorities identified the business as Local Lanes Duckpin Bowling and Eatery, which includes a restaurant, bowling alley and game room. Both men have since bonded out.

The investigation began after a security guard patrolling the property noticed something unusual and called 911. According to Budensiek, the guard came across a man at the business's back door. When the guard tried to confront him, the man ran away. The sheriff described that encounter as the initial discovery of the alleged break-in. Video from the sheriff's Air One unit showed deputies following a suspect from the air as officers searched on the ground. In the footage, a deputy directed officers toward the suspect, telling them he would be on their right and instructing them to stop their vehicle.

Deputies found one man walking along the road and another coming out of the woods with an electric scooter, according to the sheriff's account. Footage of the arrest included a deputy ordering a suspect to lie facedown on the ground. Budensiek said one of the men admitted that they had broken into the business to play video games after it had closed. According to the sheriff, the men had visited earlier and wanted to return to continue playing. That explanation, Budensiek said, was the reason one suspect gave for entering the closed business.

“They had been there earlier, had enjoyed it, were trying to come back and continue playing Pac-Man. And ended up in a serious game of hide-and-go-seek with the Martin County Sheriff's Office,” Budensiek said. His account connected the men's earlier visit and desire to play more games with the alleged burglary and the search that followed the security guard's call. The sheriff also delivered a warning to people visiting the area: “Don't come here and do stupid things; definitely don't come here and try to victimize our citizens,” he said. Schoedinger and Bolon both face felony burglary charges despite having bonded out.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County to consider Port of Fort Pierce master plan Dec. 1
hero.body:
St. Lucie County commissioners are scheduled to consider adopting the final draft of the 2026 Port of Fort Pierce Master Plan on Dec. 1, setting a long-term vision for waterfront development and helping the county seek state and federal grants for port improvements. The meeting begins at 6 p.m. in Fort Pierce.

County Port, Inlet and Beaches staff will present the plan. Commissioners can approve the document as presented or amend it before adoption, according to the county. The update supplements the port’s 2020 master plan and incorporates feedback from residents and industry stakeholders since commissioners last reviewed the draft Aug. 11. Its development proposals are part of a long-term vision, while proposed zoning changes and the Port Overlay District remain under discussion.

Among the draft’s long-term opportunities is a Launch Vehicle Recovery Facility to support offshore rocket recovery operations, including drone ships and other support vessels. The proposal is part of a broader mixed-use working waterfront vision that includes mega-yacht services, marine research, workforce training, recreation and public access. The plan calls for continued growth of mega-yacht maintenance and repair operations, along with a marina at Museum Pointe where yachts could dock temporarily for crew changes, provisioning or staging before service.

Harbour Pointe is envisioned as a public-facing district with a regional boat ramp, waterfront dining and commercial space, an entertainment pavilion, a shared-use path and a living shoreline. The update also proposes a marine research and workforce training campus focused on marine science, environmental education and training for waterfront jobs. Infrastructure and access proposals include a new road to Harbour Pointe, stormwater improvements, a possible connection to the regional Sun Trail and a future Port to Park link between the waterfront and Franklin Park.

Commissioners will consider the plan during their regular meeting in the Commission Chambers on the third floor of the Roger Poitras Administration Annex, 2300 Virginia Ave. in Fort Pierce. The meeting will also be streamed on the county’s website and YouTube channel. Residents can review the draft on the county’s Port Master Plan webpage.
